🇮🇷⚔️Iran Ship Seizures Not Ceasefire Breach, Says White House as Tensions Rise in Key Waterway

Iran’s seizure of two cargo ships in the Strait of Hormuz has not broken the current ceasefire, the White House said on Wednesday, despite video showing armed boarding by Iranian forces.

The statement followed the release of footage by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, showing its naval units stopping and taking control of two commercial ships between April 22 and 23. The vessels, named Epaminondas and MSC Francesca, were halted, boarded, and moved into Iranian waters. A third ship, Euphoria, was also hit and disabled during the same operation.

Shipping sources said the Epaminondas, registered in Liberia and managed by Technomar, suffered heavy damage to its bridge after coming under fire near Oman. The company confirmed that all 21 crew members, including workers from Ukraine and the Philippines, were safe. The MSC Francesca, registered in Panama, was forced to stop later, though no injuries or damage were reported.

Iran said the ships were seized over claimed rule breaches at sea. Panama strongly criticised the move, calling it unlawful and a serious threat to shipping safety.

Despite the rising tension, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said the actions did not break the ceasefire. “These were not American or Israeli ships, these were international vessels,” she said, adding that the US naval blockade on Iran remains “highly effective.”

The seizures are widely seen as a response to recent US actions, including the taking of Iranian ships before planned talks in Pakistan. The stand-off between Washington and Tehran has grown since joint US and Israeli strikes on Iran earlier this year.

The Strait of Hormuz, which carries about one fifth of the world’s traded energy, is now under heavy strain. Ship traffic has fallen as fears grow of further clashes, disrupting global supply chains.

Oil prices have climbed above $100 per barrel, about 35 percent higher than before the crisis, adding pressure to rising living costs worldwide.

With no clear path to talks, the risk of further disruption in this vital trade route remains high.

Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. on Thursday dismissed China’s accusations against the Philippines, challenging Beijing to substantiate its claims and ridiculing its criticism of joint military exercises.

Teodoro was reacting to China’s allegation that Philippine vessels were burning and dumping garbage at Ayungin Shoal, as well as its warning that the Philippines, the United States, and Japan were “playing with fire” through the Balikatan exercises.
